claims.claim: The Newcomen engine condensed steam by injecting a spray of cold water directly into the working cylinder, creating the vacuum for the power stroke.
claims.episode_span: The cylinder was deliberately flooded with cold water to condense the steam, then the same metal mass had to be reheated with fresh steam before the next cycle could begin.
claims.supporting_quote: The regulator valve was then closed and the water injection valve V' briefly snapped open and shut, sending a spray of cold water into the cylinder. This condensed the steam and created a partial vacuum under the piston

claims.claim: The Newcomen design's dominant loss was that the cooled cylinder walls condensed fresh steam on every stroke, so a large share of the fuel went to reheating the same metal.
claims.episode_span: Most of the heat therefore never produced mechanical work; it cycled endlessly between the boiler and the cylinder walls.
claims.supporting_quote: After the water vapor within was cooled enough to create the vacuum, the cylinder walls were cold enough to condense some of the steam as it was admitted during the next intake stroke

claims.claim: Watt moved condensation into a separate external condenser vessel connected to the cylinder by a pipe, so the working cylinder could stay hot.
claims.episode_span: moved the condensation step to a separate vessel kept cold while the working cylinder stayed hot
claims.supporting_quote: In the Watt steam engine , condensation took place in an exterior condenser unit, attached to the steam cylinder via a pipe

claims.claim: Watt surrounded the cylinder with a steam jacket to keep it warm and prevent condensation within it.
claims.episode_span: Watt also added a steam jacket around the cylinder to reduce heat loss to the surroundings
claims.supporting_quote: surround the cylinder with a jacket. Steam was passed through the jacket before being admitted below the piston, keeping the piston and cylinder warm to prevent condensation within it

claims.claim: Watt's engine burned a small fraction of the fuel of a comparable Newcomen engine: sources report figures from about half (early commercial design) to about a quarter (fully developed), a range that brackets the digest's 'roughly one-third'.
claims.episode_span: Watt’s engine reduced fuel consumption to roughly one-third that of a comparable Newcomen engine under similar lift conditions
claims.supporting_quote: As fully developed, it used about 75% less fuel than a similar Newcomen one
